bodies.name: Sun
bodies.description: The star at the center of our Solar System — a G-type main-sequence star.
facts: Accounts for 99.86% of the Solar System's mass.
Light reaches Earth in about 8 minutes 20 seconds.
Expected to remain stable for ~5 billion more years.

bodies.name: Mercury
bodies.description: Smallest planet and closest to the Sun — extreme temperature swings.
facts: No atmosphere to retain heat.
Caloris Basin is one of the largest impact craters in the Solar System.
Orbital resonance with the Sun creates a 3:2 spin-orbit lock.

bodies.name: Venus
bodies.description: Earth's twin in size — hellish greenhouse world with crushing pressure.
facts: Hottest planet in the Solar System despite not being closest to the Sun.
Rotates backwards compared to most planets.
Brightest natural object in the night sky after the Moon.

bodies.name: Earth
bodies.composition: Rocky — iron core, silicate crust, nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere
bodies.description: Our home — the only known world with liquid water oceans and life.
facts: 71% of the surface is covered by water.
Magnetic field shields life from solar radiation.
Atmosphere contains 21% oxygen.

bodies.name: Mars
bodies.description: The Red Planet — target of robotic exploration and future human missions.
facts: Olympus Mons is the tallest volcano in the Solar System.
Evidence of ancient river valleys and lakes.
Perseverance rover searches for signs of past microbial life.

bodies.name: Jupiter
bodies.composition: Mostly hydrogen and helium gas giant
bodies.description: Largest planet — a stormy gas giant that shields the inner Solar System.
facts: Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth, raging for centuries.
Strongest magnetic field of any planet.
Galilean moons discovered in 1610 changed astronomy forever.

bodies.name: Saturn
bodies.composition: Hydrogen, helium; famous icy ring system
bodies.description: Ringed jewel of the Solar System — less dense than water.
facts: Rings are mostly ice particles ranging from dust to house-sized.
Moon Titan has lakes of liquid methane.
Could float in a bathtub big enough.

bodies.name: Uranus
bodies.composition: Ice giant — water, ammonia, methane ices
bodies.description: Tilted ice giant spinning on its side — faint ring system.
facts: Axial tilt of ~98° — likely from ancient giant impact.
Methane gives it a blue-green hue.
Discovered by William Herschel in 1781.

bodies.name: Neptune
bodies.description: Windiest planet — discovered through mathematics before it was seen.
facts: Winds up to 2,100 km/h — fastest in the Solar System.
Predicted by Urbain Le Verrier from orbital wobbles of Uranus.
Moon Triton orbits backwards.

bodies.name: Pluto
bodies.description: Dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt — heart-shaped glacier on its surface.
facts: New Horizons flyby in 2015 revealed mountains of water ice.
Reclassified as dwarf planet in 2006.
Orbit crosses inside Neptune's path.

bodies.name: Ceres
bodies.description: Largest object in the asteroid belt — may have subsurface ocean.
facts: Visited by NASA Dawn spacecraft.
Contains about one-third of the asteroid belt's total mass.

bodies.name: Moon
bodies.description: Earth's only natural satellite — formed from a giant impact ~4.5 billion years ago.
facts: Same side always faces Earth (tidal locking).
Apollo missions landed 12 humans on its surface.
Drives ocean tides.

bodies.name: Io
bodies.description: Most volcanically active body in the Solar System.
facts: Sulfur volcanoes powered by Jupiter's tidal heating.
Galileo moon discovered in 1610.

bodies.name: Europa
bodies.description: Ice-covered moon with a subsurface ocean — prime astrobiology target.
facts: Europa Clipper mission will study habitability.
Surface crisscrossed by fractures.

bodies.name: Ganymede
bodies.description: Largest moon in the Solar System — bigger than Mercury.
facts: Has its own magnetic field.
Likely layered interior with ocean.

bodies.name: Titan
bodies.description: Thick atmosphere and methane lakes — Cassini-Huygens explored it.
facts: Only moon with dense atmosphere.
Huygens probe landed on its surface in 2005.

bodies.name: Enceladus
bodies.description: Ice geysers erupt from its south pole — hints of hydrothermal activity.
facts: Plumes contain water vapor and organic molecules.
Global subsurface ocean suspected.

bodies.name: Triton
bodies.description: Neptune's largest moon — captured Kuiper Belt object with nitrogen geysers.
facts: Orbits Neptune in reverse.
Surface temperature about −235 °C.

bodies.name: Phobos
bodies.description: Larger, inner Martian moon — doomed to crash into Mars in tens of millions of years.
facts: Orbits Mars three times per Martian day.
Heavily cratered and grooved.

bodies.name: Charon
bodies.description: Pluto's largest moon — forms a binary dwarf-planet system.
facts: So large relative to Pluto they orbit a common center.
Red cap at north pole from captured atmosphere.

bodies.name: Sirius
bodies.description: Brightest star in Earth's night sky — binary system 8.6 light-years away.
facts: Known as the Dog Star.
Twice as massive as the Sun.

bodies.name: Betelgeuse
bodies.description: Red supergiant in Orion — may explode as a supernova within 100,000 years.
facts: If placed at the Sun's position, it would engulf Jupiter.
Variable brightness observed since antiquity.

bodies.name: Proxima Centauri
bodies.description: Closest known star to the Sun — 4.24 light-years away with an Earth-sized planet.
facts: Red dwarf with powerful flares.
Part of the Alpha Centauri triple system.

bodies.name: Polaris
bodies.description: North Star — Cepheid variable used for navigation near the north celestial pole.
facts: Not the brightest star, but nearly aligned with Earth's axis.
About 433 light-years away.

bodies.name: Apollo 11
bodies.description: First crewed Moon landing — Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin, July 1969.
facts: Eagle landed in Mare Tranquillitatis.
Returned 21.5 kg of lunar samples.
Michael Collins orbited in Columbia.

bodies.name: Voyager 1
bodies.description: Farthest human-made object — entered interstellar space in 2012.
facts: Launched 1977.
Carries the Golden Record.
Still communicating with Earth.

bodies.name: Voyager 2
bodies.description: Only probe to visit Uranus and Neptune — also in interstellar space.
facts: Grand Tour of the outer planets.
Launched before Voyager 1 but on a slower path.

bodies.name: Hubble Space Telescope
bodies.description: Orbiting observatory revolutionizing astronomy since 1990.
facts: Imaged deep fields revealing thousands of galaxies.
Serviced by Space Shuttle astronauts.

bodies.name: James Webb Space Telescope
bodies.description: Infrared flagship observatory at the Sun–Earth L2 point.
facts: Sees the first galaxies after the Big Bang.
Sunshield the size of a tennis court.

bodies.name: Cassini–Huygens
bodies.description: Orbited Saturn 2004–2017 — studied rings, Titan, and Enceladus.
facts: Deliberately plunged into Saturn to protect moons.
Huygens landed on Titan.

bodies.name: Perseverance
bodies.description: Mars rover in Jezero Crater — collects samples for future return.
facts: Carries Ingenuity helicopter.
Searches for biosignatures in ancient lakebed.

bodies.name: International Space Station
bodies.description: Largest structure in space — continuous human presence since 2000.
facts: Orbits Earth every ~90 minutes.
Partnership of NASA, Roscosmos, ESA, JAXA, CSA.

bodies.name: Artemis program
bodies.description: NASA's return to the Moon — sustainable exploration and Mars preparation.
facts: Artemis I flew uncrewed around the Moon.
Aims to land diverse crews including first woman.

bodies.name: New Horizons
bodies.description: First flyby of Pluto — continues exploring the Kuiper Belt.
facts: Flyby on 14 July 2015.
Later visited Arrokoth, a contact-binary KBO.

bodies.name: Andromeda Galaxy
bodies.description: Nearest major galaxy — on collision course with the Milky Way in ~4.5 billion years.
facts: 2.5 million light-years away.
Contains about one trillion stars.

bodies.name: Orion Nebula
bodies.description: Stellar nursery visible to the naked eye — 1,344 light-years away.
facts: Young stars forming in dense gas clouds.
Part of the Orion constellation.

bodies.name: Milky Way
bodies.description: Our home galaxy — barred spiral with 100–400 billion stars.
facts: Solar System in the Orion Arm.
Supermassive black hole Sagittarius A* at center.

bodies.name: Crab Nebula
bodies.description: Remnant of a supernova recorded in 1054 CE.
facts: Powered by a pulsar at its center.
Expanding at 1,500 km/s.

bodies.name: Pillars of Creation
bodies.description: Iconic columns of gas in the Eagle Nebula — imaged by Hubble and Webb.
facts: About 6,500 light-years away.
Stars forming within dense dust.

bodies.name: Sagittarius A*
bodies.description: Supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way.
facts: 4 million solar masses.
First imaged by Event Horizon Telescope in 2022.

bodies.name: M87* Black Hole
bodies.description: First black hole ever photographed — 55 million light-years away.
facts: 6.5 billion solar masses.
Powers a relativistic jet thousands of light-years long.
